articleTitle: Effective computational techniques for EMC analysis of cable harness
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Effective computational techniques for Multi-Transmission Line (MTL) based on Lumped Circuit Transmission Line (LCTL) method are suggested and applied for EMC analysis of complex cable harness. Accuracy of developed algorithms is validated by comparisons with measurements.

articleTitle: Developing the information model of the reachability graph
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Information model has been developed to store data about the reachability graph. The developed model uses data structures based on double-ended lists and XML-format enabling possibility of graph structure modification and integration with other subsystems of information technologies of micromechanical system analysis and synthesis.

articleTitle: Application of argument principle for determination of number of solutions to nonlinear integral equations related to problems with free phase
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The subject of investigation is a class of nonlinear integral equations of the Hammerstein type with separated argument (phase) of unknown function, that arise particularly in the phase optimization problems. Earlier their solutions were represented by finite number of complex parameters that were determined from a system of transcendental equations. For determination of the number of solutions to this system the argument principle is used. Numerical results are presented for the particular case related to the Fourier transform.

articleTitle: Complex vanishing solutions to nonlinear integral equation related to modified phase problem
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A nonlinear integral equation of Hammerstein type arising in the so-called modified phase problem is considered. The complex vanishing solutions to this equation are investigated. Solutions of the equation are represented by means of polynomials of finite degree. Consistency of previously defined system of transcendental equations for parameters of the polynomials is proved. Numerical results are analyzed for concrete examples.

articleTitle: Compact CPW- fed antenna with semicircle on two rectangular patches for WLAN application
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This paper presents a CPW-fed antenna with a semicircle placed on two rectangular patches for WLAN application. This Antenna satisfies the licensed frequency band (5.15 to 5.95 GHz) having return loss lower than -10 dB. The antenna is designed on a substrate with dielectric constant ε<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</sub>=4.4. The size of the antenna is 16.2mm×16.1mm×1.2mm. The effects of shape, length, size, and location of feeding point, substrate and their thickness have been evaluated. Obtained 2D radiation patterns with elevation, VSWR, return loss, gain, and antenna efficiency are discussed. The simulation results of this antenna are analyzed by using Method of Moment (MoM) from IE3D software.

articleTitle: SH-wave scattering by elastic inclusion with thin interface inhomogeneity of low rigidity
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The problem of interaction of a plane time-harmonic SH-wave with an elastic inclusion of non-classical cross-sections, when an crack-like inhomogeneity is present between the infinite elastic matrix and the fiber, is considered. The method employed is a modified null field approach.

articleTitle: Nonlinear resonances in Bragg layered structures with lumped reactive elements
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Scattering of plane monochromatic waves on Bragg layered structures with nonlinear lumped inhomogeneities is considered. Exact solutions for complex amplitudes of reflected and transmitted waves are found by method of transmission matrices. Complicated hysteresis phenomena are observed for case of Kerr nonlinearity of two nonlinear elements connected into Bragg structure. Analytical expressions describing relations of incident and transmitted amplitudes in “magnitude” hysteresis are obtained.

articleTitle: Bistable wave transmission through a metal screen with a slit filled nonlinear dielectric
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: We report on a bistable wave transmission through a narrow slit with Kerr nonlinear dielectric filling which is perforated on a perfectly conducting metal screen. The approximate analytical expressions for calculation of both the inner intensity inside the slit and the transmission coefficient are presented.

articleTitle: Security system based on signals reflectometer
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The main goal of this work is construction of the special electronic devices and equipment - annunciator for guarding partition systems. The objective of this paper is consideration of the methods, permitting quick patrolling, easy intruder detection and revealing approximation of the undesirable person to the guarded object. In this paper we introduce three wires reflectometer system.

articleTitle: Reliability estimation of composite electromagnetic systems
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Main time indices for reliability estimation of composite electromagnetic systems are examined in this paper. Models are worked out for the duration of the system stay in each of it states and the average duration of the system's stay in the prescribed availability condition in the case when the lifetime of ageing output elements is circumscribed by the Raileigh distribution.

articleTitle: Modeling water level's heaving and low-frequency Electromagnetic response from the highly conductive object submering in water environment
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this paper we present simulation results, which illustrate how water level's heaving, can influence on low-frequency magnetic response of the electrically highly-conducting object placed in water environment. The time domain problem is solved using interpolation of partial solutions obtained in the frequency domain. In the frequency domain Electromagnetic problems are solved using the method of auxiliary sources. GEM sensor is modeled as excitant in the electromagnetic problem. Presented results estimate capabilities of the low frequency EMI in the detection and the discrimination of an unexploded ordinance (UXO) in water environment.

articleTitle: Interaction of ULF electromagnetic planetary wavy structures with shear flow in the rotating ionosphere
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The generation and further linear and nonlinear dynamics of planetary electromagnetic ultra-low-frequency internal waves (EULFW) are investigated in the rotating ionosphere in the presence of inhomogeneous zonal wind (shear flow). Planetary EULFW appear as a result of interaction of the ionospheric medium with the spatially inhomogeneous geomagnetic field. An effective linear mechanism responsible for the generation and intensification of large scale EULF waves in the shear flow is found. For shear flows, the operators of the linear problem are not self-adjoint, and therefore the eigen-functions of the problem maybe non-orthogonal and can hardly be studied by the canonical modal approach. Hence it becomes necessary to use the so-called nonmodal mathematical analysis. It has been shown that the shear flow driven wave perturbations effectively extract energy of the shear flow and temporally algebraic increasing own amplitude and energy. Therefore, these perturbations undergo self organization in the form of the nonlinear solitary vortex structures due to nonlinear twisting of the perturbation's front. Depending on the features of the velocity profiles of the shear flows the nonlinear vortex structures can be either monopole vortices, or dipole vortex, or vortex streets and vortex chains.

articleTitle: The electromagnetic properties of periodic structures
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Our problem is to study electromagnetic properties of complex materials. We have published the articles in this direction. In these articles there was showed that if we embed into dielectric body the lattice consisted of resonance elements, then this structure has the properties of complex media In this article there is considered the diffraction of the plane wave on the infinite periodical structure.

articleTitle: Fields compensation by two linear arrays
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Use of the compensation method for creation of a weak field area at a desired position in an antenna near region is considered. It is shown that the use of arrays of additional radiators can effectively increase the dark spot dimensions.

articleTitle: Efficient block diagonal preconditioner for boundary element method in acoustics
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: An efficient preconditioner for iterative solution of the boundary integral equations for acoustic problems is presented. This method employs the improved Burton-Miller formulation overcome non-unique problems, and avoids the numerical difficulty of evaluating the hypersingular integral. The resulting matrix equation is solved iteratively with the generalized minimal residual method (GMRES) and an efficient block diagonal preconditioner is applied to accelerate the convergence. Numerical results demonstrate the accuracy and efficiency of the developed method for acoustic problems. The fast convergence properties indicate the developed method would be a promising application of the fast multipole boundary element method for large-scale acoustic problems.

articleTitle: To the theory of electromagnetic horn antennas
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Aspects of creation of correct electrodynamic theory of horn antennas are suggested. This is demonstrated on the example of E-wave sector horn. It is shown how should be overcome the mathematical difficulties existing now in this direction.

articleTitle: Shielded transmission line with an arbitrary number of conducting strips situated in the same plane
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The construction ways of shielded multiconductor microstrip transmission line mathematical model are considered. As most perspective the mathematical model developed on the basis of singular integral equation of the first find on a set of intervals is recognized.

articleTitle: On the electrodinamics of counter propagating transverse - magnetic waves in the absorbing plate in a waveguide
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Propagation of two coherent counter propagating transverse-magnetic (TM) electromagnetic waves in the absorbing plate in the waveguide of arbitrary cross section is considered. Fresnel formulas and analytical expressions for the power reflection, transmission and transmission interference coefficients are obtained. Some aspects of tunnel interference in the absorbing plate are discussed.

articleTitle: Simulation and analysis of four- and multi-port waveguide junctions
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A rigorous electromagnetic theory is suggested to analyze characteristics of four- and multi-port waveguide junctions with a number of resonance regions. The numerical results are presented to provide the validity of the obtained solution and demonstrate the electrodynamic properties of analysed geometries.

articleTitle: A meshless method for 3-D wave propagation problems
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This paper formulates a radial basis function (RBF) meshless method for the numerical simulation of the wave propagation problems which are governed by the second-order wave equation. The spatial derivatives are approximated by RBF collocation technique whereas the temporal derivatives are discretized using the generalized trapezoidal method. Corresponding boundary conditions are enforced analytically at a discrete set of boundary nodes. The performances of the present method are demonstrated through their application to a wave propagation problem.

articleTitle: About branching of solutions of synthesis problem for a flat aperture according to the prescribed amplitude directivity pattern
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The synthesis problem of flat aperture according to the prescribed amplitude directivity pattern (DP), which is reduced to investigation and numerical solution of a two-dimensional non-linear integral equation of the Hammerstein type, is considered. The transcendental equations for finding the branching lines of the solutions are obtained. A numerical method of their finding is proposed. For the case of rectangular aperture the investigations of finding the branching-off solutions are given.

articleTitle: Asymptotic solution of em field wave scattering problem by small bodies: Numerical results
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The problem of electromagnetic wave scattering by many small bodies is reduced to solving a Fredholm second-kind integral equation. This equation is solved asymptotically as the characteristic size a of the small bodies tends to zero. The numerical calculations concern the investigation of applicability of the asymptotic formulas depending on the parameters of problem. Numerical results are presented for the case of not big number of bodies.

articleTitle: Diffraction on a hole in rotating screen
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A screen with a hole is considered. A diffraction image arises on the receiving plane located in the Fresnel zone in parallel to the screen. If the screen rotates in its plane, then the image does as well. The question is discussed what is distribution of the field energy on the receiving plane averaged over the period.

articleTitle: Comparative synthesis of waveguide array using the variational approach and R-function method
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The synthesis problem of the waveguide array according to the prescribed amplitude radiation pattern is considered. The mutual coupling of the separate elements of array is taken into account in the process of solution of a direct problem (analysis problem). Variational statement of the synthesis problem and application of the R-function method, are considered as alternative approaches to solve the synthesis problem. The functional representing a mean-square deviation of the prescribed and received radiation patterns is minimized, as well as the expansion of synthesized amplitude radiation pattern in the series by some kind of R-functions that implies the finding the expansion coefficients, are used for finding the optimal amplitude distributions of current in antenna. The corresponding nonlinear equations are reduced; and the modeling results are shown.

articleTitle: Modeling of a thin dipole antenna loaded at the ends by different diameter metal disks
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: We report on a method of numerical analysis of characteristics of a thin loaded dipole antenna. The method is applied to study a short loaded monopole with a finite size of a metal background. Numerical results are presented on frequency dependencies of an input feed current and an input impedance of the monopole for a few different values of a diameter of a metal circular background screen.

articleTitle: The compensation method and the antenna pattern
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The radiation pattern of an antenna structure used for decreasing irradiation of human organism is considered. Methods for placement of the radiators ensuring minimal distortions of the pattern in the horizontal plane are determined. The performances of the axial and lateral placements of the radiators are analyzed.

articleTitle: Microstrip antenna for dual band/wireless application
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This paper presents a micro strip antenna for dual band wireless applications. This antenna satisfies for the frequency band (1.98 to 2.08 GHz) and (2.75 to 2.78 GHz) having return loss lower than −10 dB. At first band the return loss of the antenna is −37db and at second band return loss is −19db. The antenna is designed on a substrate with dielectric constant=1.1. With a size 89mm×64mm×4mm the antenna operates for wireless applications [4], [5] for medical use. The effects of shape, length, size and location of feeding point, substrate and their thickness have been evaluated. 2D radiation pattern with elevation has been computed with VSWR < 2, Return loss > −37db, gain > 8dB, efficiency vs. frequency > 96%. The simulation results of this antenna are analyzed by using Method of Moment (MoM) [7] from IE3D software.

articleTitle: Scattering from a finite periodic array of magnetized ferrite rods
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A semi-analytical approach for electromagnetic scattering from layered cylindrical arrays is presented. The method is used to analyze the scattering of a plane wave by a finite periodic array of circular rods of magnetized ferrite.

articleTitle: Analysis of acoustical field radiated from two moving trains
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The problem of sound radiation from two trains is considered. This object has been simulated as sets of point sources uniformly distributed in domain of two lengthened rectangles moving in opposite directions. The solution of problem is obtained using integral Fourier-transforms over space coordinates and time. The integrals are calculated using the stationary phase method. Numerical analysis is performed for acoustic pressure and sound intensity.

articleTitle: Advanced computational techniques to simulate up-to-date automotive antenna EM/EMC problems
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Based on the recent enhancements of the traditional MoM, a combined set of the advanced methods, techniques and special means is proposed to provide an accurate and effective simulation of EM/EMC automotive antenna problems.

articleTitle: Speed of sound in medium in the presence of external force field and theory of gravity waves
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: It is proposed that the existing opinion about adiabaticity of sound does not reflect fully a nature of this phenomenon. It is valid only for medium, which is free of external force field. In the presence of an external force field, for example gravity, the medium becomes non-isentropic, in connection with it; possibly that the isobaric change of density is consequence of temperature fluctuation caused by fluctuation of entropy.

articleTitle: Generation and resonance scattering of waves on cubically polarisable nonlinear dielectric layer
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The analysis of the scattering problem and the generation of the third harmonic by excitation by a plane wave passing a non-linear, isotropic, cubically polarisable, non-magnetic, linearly polarised (E polarisation), layered dielectric structure is carried out. Results of the numerical investigation of both the values of the non-linear dielectric constants corresponding to given amplitude of the incident field and of the scattered and generated fields are presented.

articleTitle: Problems we chose
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: These notes are addressed to people who work at comparatively small (research or university) scientific teams. They are often met with a necessity to choose the direction and style of their investigations. Members of large scientific collectives, aimed to solve a certain applied problem, do not face this necessity. They have less degree of freedom (but bigger salary). The author doesn't know any universal criteria for above choice, and, probably they do not exist at all. Here an attempt is made to classify several situations in which such a choice should be made, and some arguments are given in behalf of different decisions. There are four typical situations, when the decision must be made, in which direction work should be continued and/or in which way it should be organized. Below the arguments are given in behalf of two possible decisions. In all these cases, the objectives “B” are preferable for the author. He understands that their advantages against the objectives “A” are improvable. Of course, the examples given below have only demonstrative (but not convincing) meaning.

articleTitle: Comparative study of the differential phase shift in some circular waveguides, containing azimuthally magnetized ferrite
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The differential phase shift, provided by two circular waveguides: the first - entirely and the second - partially filled with remanent ferrite of azimuthal magnetization, is calculated in normalized form for the normal TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01</inf> mode. In the second transmission line the anisotropic load is of the shape of a toroid which takes up its outer area only, while its interior is occupied by dielectric. Furthermore, the relative permittivities of both strata are assumed equal. The results are obtained by means of an iterative approach, based on a repeated numerical solution of the relevant characteristic equations for varying parameters, and are presented graphically. The comparative analysis performed shows that for each of the structures considered the domain in which the phase shift is produced, is finite. Besides, its size, as well as the value and the sign of phase shift, depend on the degree of filling of the configuration by dielectric (if available) and on the magnitude of the off-diagonal ferrite permeability tensor element.

articleTitle: Improved numerical simulation and analisys of thermal response duing em exposure with FDTD-Lab
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this paper we suppose to discuss recent results of study influence of Electromagnetic (EM) exposure of mobile phones radiation on a human [1]. After calculations on different existed standard frequencies, with different distances between user's head and antenna using different antenna types were conducted (all calculation are part of ongoing MMFPII research project according to the specified) it appeared that there is more information needed for analyses of thermal response than just calculating peak values of Spatial Absorption Rate (SAR) and temperature rise to be studied. In [2] it was shown, that presence and position of the hand (which is actually required in order to use the phone) substantially can change users head exposure and radiation pattern. In this paper it is shown, that during analysis exposure we could consider another parameters of the antenna's position.

articleTitle: Scattering of low frequency magnetic fields by thin 3D sheets with combined resistive and magnetic properties
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The subject of this paper is numerical modelling of thin 3D sheets with combined resistive and magnetic properties, exposed by low frequency magnetic fields. We use Mitzner's boundary conditions, written for tangential electric and magnetic fields. Scattered fields are represented only by vector potential, which is calculated based on single and double layer currents, located on the interface surface. Resulting equations are solved via Method of Moments. Numerical simulations are compared with semi-analytic solutions for thin plate and for cylindrical shell.

articleTitle: Analysis of EMC/EMI problems in printed circuit boards using Green's function approach
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In this paper application of Green's function approach for simulation of PCB structures is demonstrated. Particularly, coupling from PCB model of power inverter to glass antenna is investigated. Simulation results are compared with measurement results. A number of important advantages of the method are described.

articleTitle: Simulation-based optimization of a solar water heating system by a hybrid genetic-binary search algorithm
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: A proper design of a large solar heating system is important to maximize the benefit of the system. The system hydraulics, control parameters and dimensions of single components are usually tried to be optimized towards achieving better system performance at lower costs. The complexity of the target functions, a large number of optimization parameters and boundary conditions imposed on the system require application of advanced numerical optimization techniques and tools as well as additional software. In this paper, a hybrid genetic algorithm is proposed and applied to optimization of a solar combisystem. The hybrid algorithm couples the CHC genetic algorithm with the binary (n-ary) search method. The results of the optimizations show that the proposed algorithm is almost two times faster than the pure CHC genetic algorithm and, in separate cases, more reliable in finding the global optimum. The parallel version of the algorithm was implemented in GenOpt (generic optimization software) and applied to optimization of a solar combisystem modelled and simulated with the simulation software TRNSYS. Results of the optimization are presented in this paper.

articleTitle: Electrodynamic characteristics of the system impedance vibrator - slot radiator in a rectangular waveguide
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: The approximate analytical solution of the problem about scattering of electromagnetic waves by the system impedance vibrator - slot radiator in a rectangular waveguide is represented. The electrodynamic characteristics of the structure in question in the range of the main wave of the waveguide are given.

articleTitle: On weak solution of a boundary value problem for an infinite triangular system of elliptic equations with Robin boundary conditions
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: Weak solution of the boundary value problem for the infinite triangular system of elliptic equations with Robin boundary conditions in the domain with Lipschitz boundary was introduced. The solution by volume and layer potentials was built by means of special convolution of sequences. The obtained system of boundary integral equations is equivalent to the boundary value problem. These integral equations have the same left side operators and differ only in their right sides that contain solutions of the equations of the system with previous numbers.

articleTitle: To nonlinear dynamical processes for some piezo-electric and electrically conductive continuum media
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: In the first part, there are constructing an union form of three-dimensional (respect to spatial coordinates) nonlinear dynamical systems of partial differential equations (PDEs) which contains as particular cases Navier-Stokes' equations and system of PDE theory of elasticity and, if on continuum media acts electro-magnetic fields, Maxwell's dynamical systems too. In the second part, using an union form, there are discovered some nonlinear wave processes for elastic and piezo-electric and electrically conductive anisotropic elastic thin-walled structures.

articleTitle: 70 years to Prof. Nikolai N. Voitovich
publicationTitle: 2010 XVth International Seminar/Workshop on Direct and Inverse Problems of Electromagnetic and Acoustic Wave Theory (DIPED)
abstract: This year Prof. Nikolai N. Voitovich, a well-known scientist in the field of radio physics, antenna synthesis theory, computational mathematics, and modeling, celebrated his 70<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> anniversary.
